lines.line: Summary: A chartreuse skeleton Koopa that throws bones and builds more Dull Bones to help it; it has 1 HP, 2 attack and 1 defense, and turns up commonly in Hooktail Castle.

quoted: Dull Bones are a chartreuse variant of Dry Bones first seen in Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door.
appear commonly in Hooktail Castle
They attack by throwing bones at Mario and his partners.
A Koopa Troopa that became a skeleton.
Max HP is 1, Attack is 2, and Defense is 1.
Bone Throw (2), Build (summons Dull Bones)

lines.line: Weak points: A Hammer swing takes one out easily, and a POW Block or Koops's Power Shell is very efficient against a crowd; unlike Dry Bones, they cannot put themselves back together once they are down.

quoted: they are easily taken out by simply using the Hammer.
Using a POW Block or Koops's Power Shell is also very efficient, especially when there are many Dull Bones in battle.
Unlike Dry Bones, they cannot reassemble once they are down.

lines.line: Tips: They use Build to summon more Dull Bones, which is why Goombella says attacks that strike many at once are the most effective.

quoted: Oh, and they build reinforcements, too! Attacks that can strike multiple Dull Bones at once are the most effective.

lines.line: Tips: Besides Hooktail Castle they appear in the Glitz Pit, the Palace of Shadow and the Pit of 100 Trials, and they can drop a Dried Shroom, a Fright Mask or a POW Block.

quoted: Location(s) || Hooktail Castle, Glitz Pit, Palace of Shadow, Pit of 100 Trials (Levels 1, 4-6, 9)
Dried Shroom (drop only), Fire Flower, Fright Mask (drop only), Mushroom, POW Block (drop only)

lines.line: Summary: A large blue Cleft made of metal; the only ones are the two Iron Adonis Twins you face in the Glitz Pit, and each has 6 HP and charges for 4 damage.

quoted: The only known Iron Clefts are the two members of The Iron Adonis Twins team in the Glitz Pit.
They are large blue Clefts made of impenetrable metal.
Max HP is 6, Attack is 4
Charge (4, resists counter, Piercing)

lines.line: Weak points: No attack damages them, not even moves that bypass defense or a perfectly timed Superguard; the only known way to hurt one is Yoshi's Gulp, which hits one Iron Cleft with the other.

quoted: no attacks will do any damage to them, even moves that bypass defense and if a character executes a perfectly timed Superguard.
Yoshi's Gulp provides the only known source of damaging these Iron Clefts, as it involves hitting one of the Iron Clefts with the other.

lines.line: Tips: Gulp is Yoshi Kid's move: he swallows an enemy and spits it at another enemy.

quoted: Swallows an enemy and spits it at another enemy.

lines.line: Tips: Goombella's Tattle says the only way to beat one is to whack it with the other, and that running away may not be a bad idea; the one in green shoes is the younger brother.

quoted: If that's true, the only way to beat one is to whack it with the other one... Running away may not be a bad idea at this point.
Since this one is wearing green shoes, it must be the younger brother.

lines.line: Summary: A poisonous Pokey with 8 HP and 4 attack that can call in more of its kind; you meet it at Riverside Station and on floors 41 to 49 of the Pit of 100 Trials.

quoted: Poison Pokeys are found at the Riverside Station and in floors 41-49 of the Pit of 100 Trials.
Max HP is 8, Attack is 4, and Defense is 0.
they can summon more of them to the fight

lines.line: Weak points: Fire works well, since they are highly susceptible to burning, and the Tattle Log says to take it out quickly.

quoted: highly susceptible to burning
Take it out quickly.

lines.line: Tips: Slam, Body Throw and Bonk do 3, 4 and 5 damage and all poison you, its Pull move brings in another Poison Pokey, and poison slowly drains your HP.

quoted: Slam (3, Poison), Body Throw (4, Poison), Pull (summons Poison Pokey), Bonk (5, Poison)
If you get poisoned, your HP will slowly drain, so you may want to avoid that.

lines.line: Tips: A Poison Pokey sometimes drops a Tasty Tonic when it is beaten, which cures poison, and Goombella warns that it has spines all over, so do not touch them.

quoted: they sometimes drop a Tasty Tonic when defeated so any poisoning can be cured.
they have spines all over, so DON'T touch them.

lines.line: Summary: The giant X-Naut robot that Lord Crump drives as the boss of Chapter 2, in the Great Tree; it has 30 HP, 2 attack and 1 defense.

quoted: It serves as the primary boss of Chapter 2.
Max HP is 30, Attack is 2, and Defense is 1.
Lord Crump drives it.

lines.line: Weak points: Its rocket fists are separate targets with 2 HP and no defense; it sends them out once its own HP reaches twenty, and Flurrie's Gale Force with a perfect action command is sure to remove them.

quoted: After its HP reaches twenty, Magnus von Grapple uses its turn to separate its hands
Its fists have Max HP of 2, an Attack of 4, and Defense of 0.
Notably, the X-Fists are guaranteed to be removed from battle by Flurrie's Gale Force with a perfect action command.

lines.line: Tips: While the fists are out it can only jump and stomp the ground, hitting Mario and his partner for 2 piercing damage, which a floating Flurrie is not hurt by, and each fist hits for 4.

quoted: dealing two points of base piercing damage to both Mario and his partner (other than Flurrie, who is unaffected due to floating above the ground)
flies into a party member in one of two possible trajectories, dealing four points of base damage.
Piercing attacks are damage-based attacks in the Super Mario role-playing games that ignore all or almost all defensive capabilities of the opponent.

lines.line: Tips: If both fists are beaten, a new pair is back by its second turn afterwards; after that it picks the stomp 60% of the time and releases the fists 40%, and any fists still out when its HP runs out are defeated at once.

quoted: a new pair returns to Magnus von Grapple's arms at the beginning of its second turn afterwards
it has, every turn until it releases them, a 60% chance to use Magnus von Punish and a 40% chance to release its X-Fists again.
Any X-Fists still present when Magnus von Grapple's HP is depleted are instantly defeated.

lines.line: Summary: The Chapter 4 boss from the Creepy Steeple, fought three times with 40 HP each time and an attack of 4, then 4, then 6 in the Palace of Shadow.

quoted: is the main boss of Chapter 4.
Max HP || 40 || Attack || 4 || Defense || 0 || Location(s) || Creepy Steeple
Max HP || 40 || Attack || 4 || Defense || 0 || Location(s) || Twilight Trail, Creepy Steeple
Max HP || 40 || Attack || 6 || Defense || 0 || Location(s) || Palace of Shadow

lines.line: Weak points: In the first fight he changes into a shadowy outline of Mario once his HP drops below 20, and even if you reduce him to zero before that, he changes anyway and is left with 10 HP.

quoted: Once Doopliss' HP drops below 20, he fights by transforming himself into a shadowy outline of Mario and attacking with his moves.
Even if Doopliss' health is reduced down to zero in the first fight before he copies Mario, his transformation in the battle still happens and Doopliss will have 10 HP

lines.line: Tips: Goombella cannot tattle his name, which shows as five question marks, and learning it later is what lets Mario hurt him; partner badges such as HP Plus P or Power Plus P are switched off in the second fight.

quoted: Doopliss' name is represented by five question marks
tells him his real name, which weakens the power of his spell by making him vulnerable to Mario's attacks.
any badges that affect Mario's partners (i.e. HP Plus P or Power Plus P) are disabled during this fight

lines.line: Tips: In the Palace of Shadow rematch he hits harder: his Head Missile does 6, and he copies Mario or one of your partners and attacks as them.

quoted: In this battle, Doopliss is a bit tougher, and has the ability to transform into Mario or one of his partners, and attacking as them.
(As Himself) Head Missile (6), Transform (turns into Mario or Partner)

lines.line: Summary: The pirate skeleton who holds the Sapphire Star in Pirate's Grotto on Keelhaul Key; he has three forms of 20 HP each, 4 attack and 1 defense, and he rises again in a new form when each of the first two falls.

quoted: Cortez is the holder of the fifth Crystal Star, the Sapphire Star
alongside the other Chapter 5 characters
deep within Pirate's Grotto on Keelhaul Key.
In battle, Cortez has three forms.
Max HP is 20, Attack is 4, and Defense is 1.
His HP may seem low, but he's a spirit, so even when his HP hits 0, he'll come back.
Once this first form is defeated, Cortez transforms into a serpentine state
After his second form is defeated, Cortez abandons a body and returns to a simple floating head.

lines.line: Weak points: In his second, serpent form, hit the bone pile twice and he opens his rib cage to show a green gem; the gem has no defense and takes 1 extra damage from every attack.

quoted: Attacking the pile of bones will cause Cortez to lower his upper half, and doing so twice will cause him to open his rib cage, exposing the green gem.
This gem lacks Cortez's usual 1 defense, and additionally takes 1 more damage than usual from all attacks.

lines.line: Tips: In his last form the four weapons fight on their own; a strong attack that hits everything, such as a Thunder Rage or Vivian's Fiery Jinx, shuts them down for two turns, and Flurrie's Gale Force can blow them off the stage for good.

quoted: Using a moderately strong attack that strikes all opponents, such as a Thunder Rage item and Vivian's Fiery Jinx, can disable the weapons simultaneously.
This effect is temporary, for they reanimate themselves after two turns.
Flurrie's Gale Force, if successful (though it will not affect Cortez himself), can blow the weapons out of the stage permanently.

lines.line: Tips: In the first form he swings four weapons and can hit one or both of you each turn, and the rusty hook can poison; at 10 HP or less in the last form he eats half the audience to heal, so a swift finish beats a long fight.

quoted: Between his ensemble of weapons, Cortez can attack either one or both heroes every turn.
a rusty hook that can cause poison
If Cortez falls to 10 HP or less, he can absorb souls of the audience to restore his HP
Cortez can only absorb souls equal to half the current audience members
it is possible to defeat Cortez with a swift assault before he gets a chance to absorb the souls of the audience.

lines.line: Summary: The third time you fight Lord Crump, at Keelhaul Key in Chapter 5, he brings a platoon of X-Nauts: 30 HP a round for two rounds, 3 attack and no defense.

quoted: In this encounter, Crump uses his X-Nauts as backup.
After losing to Mario and Co for the third time
Max HP || 60 (30 per round) || Attack || 3 || Defense || 0 || Location(s) || Keelhaul Key

lines.line: Weak points: Goombella says that if you take out their leader, the X-Nauts lose the focus to attack, so go for Crump first.

quoted: If we take out their leader, though, they won't have the focus to attack. Get Crump!

lines.line: Tips: He only body-slams for 3, heals after round one, and in round two summons replacements for the X-Naut platoon the turn after they fall; Goombella warns that the X-Nauts around him are a force to be reckoned with.

quoted: Body Slam (3), Heal (this occurs after Round 1), Summon (In Round 2, Lord Crump will summon replacements for the X-Naut Platoon the following turn.)
those X-Nauts all around him are a force to be reckoned with.

lines.line: Summary: A huge mass of small Smorgs that attacks on top of the Excess Express in Chapter 6, with 50 HP, 5 attack and 1 defense; it is the only chapter boss besides the Shadow Queen that guards no Crystal Star.

quoted: When the Smorgs are cornered on the top of the train, they combine into a large Smorg horde that attacks Mario and his party.
Max HP is 50, Attack is 5, and Defense is 1.
It is the only chapter boss aside from the Shadow Queen that does not guard a Crystal Star.

lines.line: Weak points: Three tentacles (Smorg Miasmas) surround the body at the start, so defeat them first: in the GameCube game that drops the body's defense to 0, and in the Switch remake the body takes no damage until they are gone.

quoted: At the beginning of the battle, three tentacles, referred to as Smorg Miasmas, surround the main body.
Defeating the tentacles will drop the body's Defense to 0, making it easier to attack.
We won't do any damage to the main body unless we defeat the tentacles first.

lines.line: Tips: The tentacles regenerate, so Goombella says to use that time to deal heavy damage.

quoted: The tentacles will regenerate, but use that time to deal a ton of damage, OK?

lines.line: Tips: After it takes a lot of damage the tentacles change into a pincer claw that does 10 damage, against 5 for the Tentacle Slap.

quoted: After Smorg takes a significant amount of damage, the tentacles change shape into a pincer claw, which deals a large amount of damage to Mario and his partner.
Tentacle Slap (5), Pinch (10)

lines.line: Summary: The upgraded robot Lord Crump drives in the X-Naut Fortress at the end of Chapter 7, with 70 HP, 6 attack and 2 defense; it is the last boss that holds a Crystal Star.

quoted: It is the seventh Chapter Boss in the game, and the last boss to hold a Crystal Star.
Max HP is 70, Attack is 6, and Defense is 2.
Location(s) || X-Naut Fortress

lines.line: Weak points: Its X-Punch fists have 5 HP, 9 attack and no defense, Goombella says to take them down early, and Flurrie's Gale Force can blow them away.

quoted: Each X-Punch has a Max HP of 5, and Attack of 9, and a Defense of 0.
Take care of those low-HP fists early on
They deal 9 damage each and can be blown away by Flurrie's Gale Force.

lines.line: Tips: Its main attack is a drill dive from above for 6 damage to Mario and his partner, and when its HP gets low it adds machine guns.

quoted: Magnus Drill Attack (6 to Mario and Partner)
Its basic attack is a drill move that drops from above.
When the body's HP gets low, it'll also fire machine guns

lines.line: Tips: Its Rapid Fire Cannon sucks up audience members and fires them at whoever is in front for 10 hits of 3 damage, and while the fists are flying you may be hit by the fists and the body in one turn.

quoted: sucking up the audience, and then opening its front to fire audience members at whomever is in front, which deals 10 hits of three damage each.
When those fists are flying, you may get attacked by the fists and body in one turn

lines.line: Summary: Hooktail's older brother, the dragon who guards the Star Stone in the Palace of Shadow, with 80 HP, 8 attack and 2 defense; he is stronger than his sister.

quoted: being the older brother of Hooktail
He lives in the Palace of Shadow and guards the Star Stone
Max HP is 80, Attack is 8, and Defense is 2.
Gloomtail is stronger than his sister.

lines.line: Weak points: He stores power with Charge Up (+8), which warns that the 16-damage Megabreath is coming, and Goombella says to use Vivian to hide from those attacks.

quoted: Charge Up (CHARGE+8; warning for Megabreath), Megabreath (16 to Mario and Partner, Piercing)
He also stores power for some attacks, so use Vivian to hide to avoid those.

lines.line: Tips: His poison breath lasts at least ten turns and he stomps or chomps whoever is in front for 8; Earthquake does 10 piercing damage but does not work on Vivian or Flurrie.

quoted: He attacks by breathing poison on Mario and his partner (taking at least ten turns to wear off), and stomping or chomping the character in front.
His earthquake move can be dangerous, but it does not work on Vivian and Flurrie.
Poison Breath (8 to Mario and Partner, Piercing, Poison), Stomp (8), Chomp (8), Earthquake (10, Piercing; useless against Flurrie and Vivian)

lines.line: Tips: Beating him makes him cough up the chest holding the Star Stone, which unlocks the pedestals in the Palace of Shadow Tower.

quoted: After defeating Gloomtail, he coughs up the treasure chest containing the Star Stone.
guards the Star Stone, which is needed to unlock the pedestals in the Palace of Shadow Tower
